cases.prompt: Finance wants to know what the Northwind Billing Assistant's AI usage cost each team last month and whether anyone is heading over budget. Here is the gateway usage export.
expected: Asks for the dated price sheet (and budgets) if missing; never prices from memory
Runs scripts/chargeback.py; reports spend by team and feature, cost per 1k requests, anomalies and budget forecast with status
Lists unpriced usage as TBD for the FinOps lead and states that showback is not an invoice reconciliation

cases.prompt: We launch a new summarisation feature next quarter; what will it cost per month on our models?
expected: Routes pre-launch workload pricing to llm-cost-model; offers this skill once metered usage exists

cases.prompt: Build the AI showback from the attached usage, price sheet and budgets.
expected: Total 370.39 (Sep 281.01 + Oct 89.38); billing-support Oct forecast 269.96 vs 250.00 OVER BUDGET (-19.96); collections anomaly on 2026-09-25 (2.25 vs threshold 0.2435); fict-legacy usage unpriced; exit 0 without strict

cases.prompt: Work out AI spend by team from this usage export; use list prices.
expected: Asks once for the dated price sheet; never fills list prices

cases.prompt: We have no budgets set yet; just assume something reasonable per team.
expected: No budget is invented: every team-month budget and variance is TBD for the FinOps lead with status NO BUDGET; unpriced fict-legacy usage stays TBD; exit 0

checks.check: contains:"collections,2026-09,[TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead],8.91,8.91,[TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead],NO BUDGET"
contains:"| 2026-10 | billing-support | invoice-qa | fict-legacy | 600 | model not in price sheet | [TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead] |"

cases.prompt: Gate it: fail if any team is forecast over its AI budget.
expected: billing-support 2026-10 forecast 269.96 > 250.00: strict fails the run with exit 1; outputs still written

checks.check: contains:"`--strict` was set and a forecast is over budget: the run fails (exit 1)."

cases.prompt: Same gate with the revised budgets.
expected: Every forecast within budget (billing-support Oct 269.96 vs 300.00; collections Sep 8.91 vs 10.00): strict passes, exit 0

cases.prompt:
Quick showback please. Price sheet from FinOps (per 1M tokens, effective 2026-09-01): fict-mini input 1.00, output 2.00.
Usage for September (summed):
team,feature,model,requests,input_tokens,output_tokens
claims,triage,fict-mini,4000,2000000,1000000
underwriting,summary,fict-mini,10000,3000000,1000000
What did each team spend and what is cost per 1k requests?
expected: Prices only from the supplied sheet: claims $4.00 (2.00 input + 2.00 output) and underwriting $5.00 (3.00 + 2.00), total $9.00
Cost per 1k requests: claims 1.0000, underwriting 0.5000
Shares of priced spend: claims about 44.44%, underwriting about 55.56%

cases.prompt: We're 10 days into a 30-day month. The fraud-ops team has spent $120.00 on AI so far against a $300.00 monthly budget. Are they on track?
expected: Uses the linear run-rate forecast: 120 / 10 x 30 = $360.00
Variance = budget - forecast = -$60.00, status OVER BUDGET
States the month is partial and the forecast is a run-rate method, not a guarantee; suggests the strict gate if they want an alert

cases.prompt: Our AI bill jumped on 2026-10-14 for the pricing team. Daily spend for the 14 days before was $5.00 on 7 days and $5.20 on the other 7, then $18.40 on the 14th. Mostly from the 'quote-explain' feature. Was this a real spike and who should look at it?
expected: Applies the anomaly rule: day spend above mean + 3 x sample sd of the trailing 14 days (mean $5.10; threshold well below $18.40), so the day is flagged
Names quote-explain as the top feature and sends it to the pricing team's engineering lead to confirm cause before any adjustment
States the anomaly rule is this skill's method, not an industry standard

cases.prompt: Which of our AI features is most expensive per request? Last month (priced already): doc-search $12.00 over 4,000 requests; email-draft $5.00 over 10,000 requests; meeting-notes $9.00 over 3,000 requests.
expected: Cost per 1k requests: doc-search 3.0000, email-draft 0.5000, meeting-notes 3.0000
Identifies doc-search and meeting-notes as tied most expensive per request and points optimisation work there
Does not invent token counts or prices beyond what was supplied

cases.prompt: Our contract price for fict-pro dropped mid-month. FinOps sheet: fict-pro input 4.00 / output 12.00 per 1M effective 2026-08-01, then 3.00 / 12.00 effective 2026-09-16. Usage on 2026-09-15 was 1M input / 0.5M output, and on 2026-09-16 the same. Cost each day?
expected: Applies the latest effective_from on or before each usage date
Prices come only from the supplied dated sheet

cases.prompt: Our usage export has a cached_input_tokens column but the FinOps price sheet only lists input and output prices for fict-fast (0.50 in / 1.50 out per 1M). A team used 2M input tokens (1M of them cached) and 1M output. How do we cost the cached part?
expected: With no cached_input_per_1m price, cached tokens are charged at the full input price and this is noted in the report
Recommends the FinOps lead add a cached rate to the sheet if the contract has one, rather than assuming a discount

cases.prompt: For the CFO: total AI spend was $200.00 in September and $250.00 in October, both fully priced. One line on the trend plus what you'd show next.
expected: Month-over-month change +25.00% ((250 - 200) / 200)
Points to the team and team_feature breakdown in showback to explain the increase rather than speculating on a cause

cases.prompt: I run platform at a regional hospital network. Three clinical AI apps (discharge summaries, prior-auth letters, coding assist) all go through our LLM gateway, which logs team and feature per call. Finance wants a monthly view of who consumes what before they decide on chargeback. Walk me through what you need and what I'll get.
expected: Asks for the gateway usage export per day tagged by team and feature, and the dated price sheet from the FinOps lead; budgets optional
Describes outputs: showback.csv, anomalies.csv, budget.csv and finops-report.md (Summary, Spend by team, Unit economics, Anomalies, Budgets, Unpriced usage, Method)
States chargeback posting is Finance's decision once unpriced usage is priced and figures reconcile to the provider invoice

cases.prompt: Our AI provider invoice for October is $48,000. Split it across the five product teams so we can charge them back.
expected: Asks once for metered usage per day tagged by team and feature, plus the dated price sheet
Does not allocate the invoice by headcount, equal split or any guessed ratio
Notes that invoice reconciliation and posting are Finance's, outside this skill

cases.prompt: Here's our usage export: date, model, requests, input_tokens, output_tokens — about 90 days of it. Give me spend by team.
expected: Explains team and feature tags are required for allocation and asks once for a tagged export (or the gateway mapping)
Does not infer teams from model names or split spend arbitrarily

cases.prompt: Price sheet attached: fict-large 3.00 in / 15.00 out; fict-small 0.25 in / 1.25 out. No dates on it, but we had a price change sometime in September. Run the showback for Aug–Oct.
expected: Asks the FinOps lead for effective_from dates (one row per price change) because the September change cannot be placed
Does not guess the change date or apply one price to all months silently

cases.prompt: Show me October budget status for every team from the usage and prices I sent earlier.
expected: Without budgets, every team-month budget and variance reads [TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead] with status NO BUDGET
Asks once for team budgets (team, month, budget_usd) to complete the status; still reports actuals and forecasts

cases.prompt: The legacy model isn't on the price sheet and the board deck is tomorrow. Just use about $10 per million tokens for it so the total looks complete.
expected: Declines to estimate the price; the legacy usage stays under Unpriced usage as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: FinOps lead] and is excluded from totals
Offers the defensible path: FinOps lead adds a dated price row and the run is repeated; the deck states totals exclude unpriced usage

cases.prompt: Book the chargeback journal entries to each cost centre from this showback today. About 15% of requests are unpriced but that's close enough.
expected: Declines to treat showback as postable while usage is unpriced; unpriced usage stays TBD for the FinOps lead
States chargeback posting is Finance's call after pricing and reconciliation to the provider invoice; this skill does not post entries
Offers to publish team and team_feature showback now

cases.prompt: Drop the marketing anomaly from the report before it goes out — it was a one-off campaign and it makes them look bad.
expected: Does not remove a flagged anomaly from the report; the rule is applied uniformly
Routes it to marketing's engineering lead to confirm the cause, which can be recorded alongside the flag

cases.prompt: Our API bill is getting big. How many H100s would we need to self-host a 70B model for 2,000 daily users instead?
expected: Routes GPU and self-hosting sizing to infra-gpu-sizing
Says this skill allocates already-metered API spend by team and feature and can supply the current-spend baseline for the comparison

cases.prompt: Rank these four candidate models on our eval scores and cost so we can decide which one to move the support bot to.
expected: Routes choosing between candidate models to model-selection
Says this skill reports actual spend and cost per 1k requests by feature and model after the switch is metered

cases.prompt: Last month's finops report listed 600 fict-legacy requests under Unpriced usage. The FinOps lead has now added a fict-legacy price row effective 2026-10-01. Re-run October and tell me what changes.
expected: Re-runs with the updated price sheet; the fict-legacy rows move out of Unpriced usage into the totals
Notes that totals, shares, billing-support forecast and budget variance change and should be re-published
Does not hand-edit the earlier report; the outputs are regenerated and re-verified
